name: Samuel P. Taylor State Park
tagline: One flat, shaded creekside path. Nothing else, but it is a good one.
summary: Samuel P. Taylor is a redwood canyon in West Marin with one route for dogs: the paved Cross Marin Trail, which runs about 3 miles along Lagunitas Creek through the whole park. Add a campground under the redwoods and a shady picnic grove and you have a relaxed weekend. You do not get the Pioneer Tree loop, Barnabe Peak or any other trail, and your dog can never go in the creek.
verdict: Bring your dog for camping and an easy creekside walk, and use it as a base for the dog beaches around Point Reyes Station. Leave them home if you want to climb Barnabe Peak.

glance.note: Cross Marin Trail only; no dirt trails
Main campground; not the cabins or the hike-and-bike site
No pets in the park cabins; pet rooms in Olema and Point Reyes Station
Dogs may never enter Lagunitas Creek
No pet fee; day-use fee per car at the entrance

allowed.name: Cross Marin Trail
allowed.detail: A paved former railroad bed that follows Lagunitas Creek the length of the park, about 3 miles, almost level and shaded by redwoods. Shared with bikes and strollers.

allowed.name: Main campground
allowed.detail: Leashed dogs are welcome at the standard family campsites in the creekside redwoods.

allowed.name: Day-use picnic grove
allowed.detail: Tables, barbecues and lawn under the redwoods beside the creek, just inside the entrance. Dogs on leash.

allowed.name: Paved roads and parking lots
allowed.detail: Sir Francis Drake Boulevard runs through the park, but it is busy and has no shoulder. Stick to the Cross Marin Trail.

allowed.name: Nearby: Point Reyes National Seashore beaches
allowed.detail: Limantour, Kehoe and the north end of Point Reyes Beach allow leashed dogs, 20 to 30 minutes away. Rules change seasonally for nesting birds, so check the seashore site.

notAllowed.name: All dirt trails
notAllowed.detail: Pioneer Tree Trail, Barnabe Peak, Ridge Trail, North Creek Trail, Bill's Trail and the Devil's Gulch area are closed to dogs.

notAllowed.name: Lagunitas Creek
notAllowed.detail: Dogs may not enter the water at any time. The creek has coho salmon and steelhead, and people are kept out from December 1 to June 15 as well.

notAllowed.name: Madrone cabins
notAllowed.detail: The six park cabins do not take pets.

notAllowed.name: Hike-and-bike campsite
notAllowed.detail: The shared site for cyclists and walkers is no-dogs.

hikes.name: Cross Marin Trail, picnic area to the north boundary
hikes.why: Flat, shaded and next to the creek the whole way. Turn around whenever you like. Winter and spring are loudest, when the creek is full.
hikes.maps: Cross Marin Trail, Samuel P. Taylor State Park

hikes.name: Cross Marin Trail, south from the campground
hikes.why: Quieter than the picnic-area end. Starts right from the campground, so no need to drive.
hikes.maps: Samuel P. Taylor State Park Campground

hangouts.name: Redwood picnic grove
hangouts.why: Deep shade, picnic tables and a lawn by the creek. The nicest place in the park to sit with a dog on a hot day.

hangouts.name: Cross Marin Trail bridges
hangouts.why: Several footbridges over the creek where you can watch the water. Stay on the bridge; no paws in the creek.

hangouts.name: Point Reyes Station
hangouts.why: 15 minutes west. Dog-friendly patios and shops, and the start of the road out to Limantour Beach.

hangouts.name: Upton Beach, Stinson Beach
hangouts.why: About 35 minutes south. The county end of Stinson Beach, where leashed dogs are allowed on the sand.

rules: Keep your dog on a leash no longer than 6 feet at all times.
Dogs may use the Cross Marin Trail, the campground, the picnic area and paved areas only. No other trails.
Dogs may never go in Lagunitas Creek, even on a leash.
At night your dog must sleep inside your tent or vehicle.
Never leave a dog unattended at a campsite or in a car.
Pick up waste and put it in a bin; do not leave bags on the trail.
Quiet hours in the campground are 10 pm to 6 am, and that includes barking.
No pets in the cabins or at the hike-and-bike site; this is enforced at booking.

camping.name: Samuel P. Taylor main campground
camping.note: About 60 sites under the redwoods beside Lagunitas Creek. Reserve on ReserveCalifornia up to 6 months ahead. Leashed dogs OK at standard sites.

camping.name: Creekside loop sites
camping.note: Closest to the water. Some reports say these sites close for flooding in winter; check when booking.

lodging.name: Olema House at Point Reyes, Olema
lodging.note: 10 minutes west. Takes 2 dogs in designated rooms for a per-dog fee; dogs cannot be left alone in rooms.

lodging.name: Olema Cottages, Olema
lodging.note: Listed as pet-friendly. Confirm the policy when you book.

lodging.name: Dancing Coyote Beach Cottages, Inverness
lodging.note: On Tomales Bay, 25 minutes away. Pet-friendly cottages.

lodging.name: Vacation rentals in Point Reyes Station and Inverness
lodging.note: Many allow dogs for a nightly fee. Check each listing.

boarding.name: Point Reyes Animal Hospital
boarding.note: Offers pet boarding in Point Reyes Station; reserve ahead if you want a dog-free day on the Point Reyes trails.

seasons.title: Winter and spring
seasons.detail: The creek runs high and the redwoods drip. Best time for the Cross Marin Trail, but expect mud on the shoulders and some campsite closures after big storms.

seasons.title: Summer
seasons.detail: Cool under the trees even when inland Marin is hot. The campground fills every weekend; book early.

seasons.title: Fall
seasons.detail: Quietest season. Dry trail, warm afternoons, cold nights in camp.

seasons.title: Creek closure
seasons.detail: Creek access is closed to everyone from December 1 to June 15 for spawning salmon. Dogs are banned from the water all year.

wildlife: Coho salmon and steelhead spawn in Lagunitas Creek. Keeping dogs out of the water is the law, not a suggestion.
Raccoons raid campsites at night. Put dog food in the car or the food locker.
Ticks live in the tall grass along the trail edges. Check your dog after each walk.
Poison oak grows along the Cross Marin Trail margins.
checklist: A 6-foot leash, not a retractable one; the trail is shared with bikes
Water and a bowl for the walk; the creek is off limits
A towel and a tick comb
A rain shell for your dog in winter; the canyon is wet for months
Food locker space or a car for dog food at night
Your ReserveCalifornia confirmation showing a pet on the booking
